title: Permission Graph Spec and SIEM Integration Roadmap
summary: Working design doc for RBAC v2 permission-graph model, audit log schema aligned to ECS, evidence automation hooks, and phased SIEM export/rollout plan. Emphasis on incremental migration with canaries and measurable KPIs.
content:
Purpose:
This working doc captures the proposed permission-graph-based RBAC v2 design (ABAC-friendly), the canonical audit log schema intended for our SIEM, and an operational rollout plan that minimizes user disruption while enabling automated evidence collection for compliance. It is explicitly iterative — expect follow-ups and smaller PRDs for each subsection.

Context / Why change:
- Current RBAC (v1) is role-list centric and tightly coupled to legacy service tokens and project IDs.
- Observed gaps: coarse-grained roles, inconsistent audit events across services, and weak signals for automated evidence generation.
- Goals: move to a graph-first model that supports attribute-based constraints, consistent high-fidelity audit events, and exportable evidence artifacts for SOC / compliance audits.

High-level design principles:
- Graph primitives (subjects, resources, actions, bindings) over large static role lists.
- Deterministic, policy-evaluation-first: PDP (policy decision point) is authoritative and emits the canonical audit event.
- ABAC optionality: attributes (dept, env, customer_tier, cost_center) used to scope policies without exploding role combinatorics.
- Backwards-compatible mapping layer for legacy roles during migration.
- Audit-first: every PDP decision must emit a single JSON event with a stable schema.

Permission graph model (initial spec):
- Nodes:
  - Subject: {type: user | service | group, id, attrs[]}
  - Resource: {type: model | deployment | project | route | secret | billing-obj, id, attrs[]}
  - Action: {name: invoke | read | write | manage | admin | audit | list}
- Edges:
  - grant(subject, action, resource, constraints?, binding-meta?)
  - inherit(group -> user), delegation(service-account -> user)
- Policy entity:
  - policy_id, expression (satisfiable over subject and resource attrs), effect (allow/deny), priority, owner, detectors (for evidence automation)
- Attribute examples:
  - subject.dept, subject.team, subject.is_service_account, subject.trust_level
  - resource.env (prod/staging/dev), resource.owner_team, resource.customer_tier

Policy evaluation flow (runtime):
1) PEP (service) sends authorization query to PDP with: request_id, actor, actor_attrs snapshot, action, resource_id, resource_attrs snapshot, callsite metadata (region, latency budget).
2) PDP evaluates policies (cache lookups first, then policy engine) -> decision {allow|deny|conditional} + policy_ids + explanation.
3) PDP returns decision and emits canonical audit event (see schema below).
4) PEP enforces decision. Conditional decisions include obligations (e.g., require_mfa, log_evidence).

Caching and scale notes:
- Deterministic caching keyed by signature(requester-id, resource-id, action, relevant-attr-hash) with TTL and invalidation hooks (policy change webhooks).
- Stale-safe: PEP may fall back to revalidate on suspect-response (mismatch between cached decision and enforcement context).

Canonical audit log schema (single-line JSON, newline-delimited) - fields we will export to SIEM (ECS-aligned where possible):
- timestamp: ISO8601
- request_id: UUID
- trace_id: optional string
- actor_id: string (user:<id> | svc:<id>)
- actor_type: user | service | group
- actor_attrs: comma-separated k=v pairs (short) or base64 blob for large attrs
- action: string (invoke/read/write/manage)
- resource_type: string
- resource_id: string
- resource_attrs: comma-separated k=v pairs (short)
- decision: allow | deny | conditional
- policy_ids: comma-separated policy ids
- policy_snapshot_hash: short(8) hash representing the set of rules evaluated
- reason: short text (first-party explanation for decision)
- latency_ms: integer (decision eval ms)
- pdp_host: hostname
- cache_hit: true|false
- request_payload_hash: sha256
- evidence_refs: comma-separated artifact ids (snapshot-UUIDs) if any were collected as part of obligation
- environment: aws/eu-west-1 / self-hosted etc.
- index_tags: list string (comma-separated) used by SIEM for fast queries (sensitivity=high,account:1234)

Mapping to SIEM (export format and pipeline):
- Export format: NDJSON (newline-delimited JSON) with ECS-compatible field names added by an enrichment stage.
- Ingest pipeline recommended:
  1) Lightweight forwarder (Fluent Bit) -> S3/GCS buffer OR direct to Logstash/ELK ingest endpoints.
  2) Enrichment lambda: attach cloud metadata, normalize actor -> user.email when available, expand resource tags into ECS labels.
  3) Parser job: map our canonical fields to ECS (e.g., actor_id -> user.id, resource_id -> url.path or host.name depending on type).
  4) Index in SIEM with daily indices and retention policies aligned to compliance.
- Minimum viability fields in SIEM (for SOC use-cases): actor_id, action, resource_type, resource_id, decision, timestamp, policy_ids, evidence_refs, index_tags.

Evidence automation hooks (how to generate artifacts referenced in audit events):
- Evidence types we will capture on demand or by obligation:
  - config_snapshot: service config and policy version (tar.gz, signed)
  - access_snapshot: list of bindings evaluated for the request (policy_ids + resolved principals)
  - request_dump: sanitized request payload (with PII redaction)
  - env_snapshot: deployment manifest + host image id + container digest
  - approval_record: for admin actions, capture approver id + timestamp + justification
- Automation flow:
  - Obligation signals from PDP (e.g., require_snapshot=true) cause PDP to trigger evidence worker async.
  - evidence worker collects artifacts from configured endpoints (k8s api, config store, audit-store), signs them with service key, stores to secure bucket with short-lived url, and returns evidence_refs to PDP.
  - Evidence_ref format: evidence://bucket/uuid?sig=xxx (short token) and hash included in audit event.
- Security / retention:
  - Evidence artifacts are encrypted with customer-managed KMS when applicable and retention TTL is set by policy.

Rollout plan (phased):
Phase 0: Tech spike + PoC (complete)
- Small PoC for a single service (inference-api) to validate PDP/PEP latency and a minimal audit event.

Phase 1: Pilot (Q4 2024) - non-prod + canary users
- Scope: deployments in staging + non-prod and a small group of internal teams (Platform, Console).
- Tasks: 1) Deploy PDP as sidecar + centralized policy store; 2) Emit canonical audit events to a private SIEM index; 3) Enable evidence obligations for admin workflows only.
- Metrics: PDP median latency < 8ms for cached, p95 < 40ms; audit-event completeness 99%; evidence generation success rate > 95%.

Phase 2: Gradual prod rollout (Q1 2025) - selective services
- Scope: onboarding low-risk production services (analytics, optimize) with read-only/low-impact actions.
- Migration strategy: dual-eval mode where PEP queries both v1 and PDP; decisions compared and discrepancies logged but not enforced.
- Create a discrepancy dashboard (Confluence + Grafana) used by owners to reconcile mismatches.

Phase 3: Enforcement and broad rollout (Q2 2025)
- Risks: service latency, incorrect deny rules causing outages.
- Controls: gradually flip enforcement for a service after 7 days of stable discrepancy rate < 0.1% and manual sign-off by service owner.
- Provide rollback path: dynamic feature-flag to revert enforcement to v1 for a given service/region.

Phase 4: Enterprise features and SIEM integration (post-rollout)
- Enable evidence obligations across higher-risk actions, export normalized events to customer SIEM integrations, and provide canned dashboards for auditors.

Migration helpers and mechanics:
- Legacy role mapping table: CSV mapping legacy_role -> policy_id(s) with flags: inherit|exclusive|translated. This is the canonical translation input during migration scripts.
- Idempotent migration script behaviors: create bindings only if not present; mark migrated bindings with metadata tag:migrated-from=v1-date.
- Backfill plan for historical audit events: run enrichment pipeline to remap legacy actor ids and annotate events with new policy_ids where feasible.

Testing checklist (minimal acceptance):
- Unit tests for policy semantics that cover allow/deny/conditional and attribute predicates.
- Load test: 10k auth QPS across PDP cluster; median decision latency < 15ms on target infra.
- Integration tests: end-to-end PEP->PDP->audit pipeline exercise with SIEM ingest in staging.
- Chaos test: flip feature-flag causing forced deny for a single low-traffic endpoint and verify rollback.

Operational KPIs to monitor:
- auth.qps, auth.latency.{p50,p95,p99}, audit.events.count, evidence.success_rate, discrepancy.rate (v1 vs v2), policy.update.latency
- Security KPIs: number of high-severity denied attempts, unusual-pattern alerts from SIEM derived from our events

Open questions / decisions needed (short term):
- Attribute propagation: what is the canonical source of truth for subject.attrs (IdP vs internal directory)? action: Security + IAM to pick by 2024-10-01.
- Evidence costs: retention and S3 egress costs for evidence artifacts —finance to provide limits.
- SIEM mapping: which customer-facing fields must we guarantee for export (customers may require email/user.email).
- Policy language: should we standardize on Rego (OPA) or a simpler internal DSL? Pro/con analysis required.

Next steps / immediate TODOs:
- (Aisha) Draft a small Rego prototype for a conditional policy example: "allow invoke on deployment if subject.trust_level >= 3 and resource.env == 'prod' and request.from_region == resource.region" (due 2024-10-10).
- (Marco) Wire up NDJSON export from PoC pipeline to staging SIEM index and validate mappings (due 2024-09-30).
- (Helen) Draft migration mapping CSV template and circulate to service owners (due 2024-10-07).
- (Priya) Cost estimate for evidence storage/retention with finance (due 2024-10-14).

Notes to reviewers: this doc intentionally mixes design and ops runway items. Please comment inline on trade-offs (Rego vs DSL, caching TTL defaults) and flag any service-specific constraints your team expects.

Appendix (short examples):
- Example policy (pseudo-Rego):
  package rbac
  allow {
    input.action == "invoke"
    input.resource.type == "deployment"
    input.subject.attrs.trust_level >= 3
    input.resource.attrs.env == "prod"
  }

- Example audit event (NDJSON single line):
{"timestamp":"2024-10-01T15:12:34Z","request_id":"6a7f8d2e-...","actor_id":"user:ajones","actor_type":"user","actor_attrs":"dept=platform,team=serving","action":"invoke","resource_type":"deployment","resource_id":"deploy-42","decision":"allow","policy_ids":"pol-1982","policy_snapshot_hash":"c3f1a5b2","reason":"matched pol-1982","latency_ms":5,"pdp_host":"pdp-1.prod","cache_hit":true,"evidence_refs":"evidence://sec-eu/uuid-1234"}

Change log: initial draft 2024-09-12 (PoC notes appended 2024-09-30), pilot plan added 2024-10-15, metrics and evidence automation details refined 2024-11-03.

End.
